items.title: Location, Extent, Regions & Relief
items.body:
## Location & extent

- After the **2014 bifurcation** (Telangana separated), Andhra Pradesh lies on India's **south-east coast** along the **Bay of Bengal**.
- Area **~1,62,970 sq km** — the **8th largest** state; **10th** by population (4.09% of India, 2011).
- Two regions: **Coastal Andhra** and **Rayalaseema**; the **north-coastal belt** (Srikakulam-Vizianagaram-Visakhapatnam) is often treated as a distinct sub-region.

## Districts (current)

- Districts rose from **13 → 26** on **4 April 2022**, then to **28** with **Polavaram** and **Markapuram** (in force **31 December 2025**).
- The AP Socio-Economic Survey 2024-25 and ISFR 2023 still list **26** — now outdated. A proposed **Madanapalle** district was **not** created (became only a headquarters).

## Physiography (three divisions)

| Division | Character |
|---|---|
| **Coastal plains** | Fertile east-coast plains; Godavari-Krishna deltas |
| **Eastern Ghats** | Discontinuous hills on the Deccan margin (Nallamala, Papikonda, Seshachalam, Erramala) |
| **Rayalaseema plateau** | Semi-arid Deccan interior |

- Highest point: **Arma Konda (~1,680-1,690 m)**, Alluri Sitharama Raju district — the **tallest peak of the Eastern Ghats**.
keyPoints: AP lies on India's south-east (Bay of Bengal) coast; ~1,62,970 sq km, 8th largest state, 10th by population.
Two regions: Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema (north-coastal Srikakulam-Vizianagaram-Visakhapatnam a distinct sub-region).
Districts: 13 → 26 (4 April 2022) → 28 with Polavaram & Markapuram (31 December 2025); the 2024-25 survey still shows 26.
Three physiographic divisions: coastal plains, Eastern Ghats, and the Rayalaseema plateau.
Arma Konda (~1,680-1,690 m), in Alluri Sitharama Raju district, is AP's highest point and the tallest Eastern Ghats peak.
items.source: AP Socio-Economic Survey 2024-25; List of districts of Andhra Pradesh (28, verified); Geography of India (Arma Konda 1,690 m)

items.title: Coastline & Ports
items.body:
## Coastline

- AP's coastline is about **974 km** along the Bay of Bengal — the **longest on India's east coast** (survey terms it the third-longest in the country).
- The coast is low and deltaic in the centre (Godavari-Krishna) and more rocky/embayed in the north (Visakhapatnam).

## Ports

- **Major (Central) port:** **Visakhapatnam** — a deep natural harbour and India's oldest shipyard hub on the east coast.
- **Non-major / other ports:** **Krishnapatnam, Gangavaram, Kakinada, Machilipatnam** (and other minor ports) support cargo, fishing and industry.
- The long coast underpins AP's fisheries, aquaculture (shrimp export leadership) and port-led industrial corridors.
keyPoints: AP coastline ≈ 974 km — the longest on India's east coast.
Visakhapatnam is AP's sole major (Central-government) port, a natural harbour.
Non-major ports: Krishnapatnam, Gangavaram, Kakinada, Machilipatnam.
The coast supports fisheries, aquaculture and port-led industry.
items.source: AP Socio-Economic Survey 2024-25; Transport in Andhra Pradesh (974 km, verified)

items.title: Rivers, River-sharing & Irrigation Projects
items.body:
## River system

- AP has **~40 major, medium and minor rivers**, of which **15 are inter-state**; all prominent rivers flow **east into the Bay of Bengal**.
- Most prominent: **Godavari, Krishna, Pennar (Penna), Vamsadhara, Nagavali**.

## River-sharing (inter-state)

| River | Shared with |
|---|---|
| **Godavari** ('Dakshina Ganga', largest peninsular river) | Maharashtra, Odisha, Karnataka, Chhattisgarh, MP |
| **Krishna** | Maharashtra, Karnataka |
| **Pennar (Penna)** | Karnataka |
| **Vamsadhara, Nagavali, Bahuda** | Odisha (north-coastal) |
| **Budameru, Errakalava, Tammileru** | Telangana |

## Major projects

- **Polavaram** — a **National Project** on the **Godavari**; AP's flagship multipurpose scheme.
- **Nagarjuna Sagar & Srisailam** — on the **Krishna**.
- **Somasila** — on the **Pennar**.
- **Handri-Neeva Sujala Sravanthi** — lifts **Krishna** water to drought-prone **Rayalaseema**.
keyPoints: AP has ~40 rivers (15 inter-state); all major rivers drain east into the Bay of Bengal.
Godavari (largest peninsular river, 'Dakshina Ganga') is shared with Maharashtra, Odisha, Karnataka, Chhattisgarh and MP.
Krishna is shared with Maharashtra & Karnataka; Pennar with Karnataka; Vamsadhara/Nagavali with Odisha.
Polavaram is a National Project on the Godavari; Nagarjuna Sagar & Srisailam are on the Krishna; Somasila on the Pennar.
Handri-Neeva lifts Krishna water to Rayalaseema.
items.mnemonic: Delta duo = Godavari + Krishna; Rayalaseema lifeline = Handri-Neeva.

figure.alt: Andhra Pradesh rivers and their major irrigation projects
figure.caption: Rivers drain east to the Bay of Bengal: Godavari (Polavaram), Krishna (Nagarjuna Sagar, Srisailam), Pennar (Somasila); Handri-Neeva serves Rayalaseema.

items.title: Climate, Agro-climatic Zones, Soils & Land Use
items.body:
## Climate

- Broadly **tropical**: the **coast is hot-humid and highly cyclone-prone** (Bay of Bengal); **Rayalaseema (esp. Anantapuramu) is semi-arid and drought-prone**.
- Most rain from the **south-west monsoon**, with a useful **north-east (retreating) monsoon** contribution on the **south coast** (Oct-Dec).

## Six agro-climatic zones

- **North Coastal, Godavari, Krishna, Southern, Scarce Rainfall** (Kurnool + Anantapuramu) and **High Altitude & Tribal Areas**.

## Soils

- Mixtures of sand, silt and clay; of **22 categories, ten predominate** (>88% of area).
- **Deltaic/coastal alluvial** (Godavari-Krishna deltas, paddy), **black cotton (regur)** on the Deccan/Rayalaseema, and **red loamy/sandy** soils in the interior.

## Land use (2023-24)

| Category | Share |
|---|---|
| Net area sown | ~30.4% |
| Recorded forest | ~22.63% |
| Current fallows | ~14.9% |
| Non-agricultural use | ~12.84% |
| Barren/uncultivable | ~8.19% |

- Total geographical area ~162.97 lakh ha.
keyPoints: AP climate is tropical: cyclone-prone humid coast vs semi-arid, drought-prone Rayalaseema (Anantapuramu driest).
South coastal districts also gain rain from the north-east (retreating) monsoon.
Six agro-climatic zones; the Scarce Rainfall zone = Kurnool + Anantapuramu.
Main soils: deltaic/coastal alluvial, black cotton (regur), and red loamy/sandy.
Land use (2023-24): net sown area ~30.4% (largest); recorded forest ~22.63%; total area ~162.97 lakh ha.
items.source: AP Socio-Economic Survey 2024-25 (agro-climatic zones, soils, land use); IMD AP climate profile

items.title: Minerals & Forests (ISFR 2023)
items.body:
## Minerals — 'Ratna Garbha'

- AP is called **'Ratna Garbha'** (womb of gems) for diverse minerals: **crude oil, natural gas, barytes, heavy mineral beach sands, manganese, limestone, dolomite, iron ore, gold, diamonds, mica, uranium, lead, zinc, granite**.
- **Mangampeta (YSR Kadapa)** — among the **world's largest barytes** deposits.
- **Thummalapalli (YSR Kadapa)** — **uranium**; **Chimakurthy (Prakasam)** — **black granite**; iron ore in Anantapuramu/Kurnool/Kadapa etc.

## Forests (ISFR 2023)

- **Forest cover** (satellite): **30,084.96 sq km = 18.46%** of area (VDF 1.22%, MDF 8.42%, OF 8.82%).
- **Recorded/notified forest area**: **37,221.11 sq km = 22.84%** — a distinct, larger administrative figure.
- **Alluri Sitharama Raju** district has the **largest forest cover** (~6,917 sq km); **Guntur** among the least.
- **Mangroves**: **~418 sq km** — India's **second-largest** after the Sundarbans, in the **Godavari & Krishna estuaries** (Coringa is the main sanctuary).
keyPoints: AP = 'Ratna Garbha'; minerals include barytes, oil/gas, beach sands, limestone, iron ore, uranium, granite, diamonds.
Mangampeta (YSR Kadapa) is among the world's largest barytes deposits; uranium at Thummalapalli; black granite at Chimakurthy.
ISFR 2023: forest cover 18.46% vs recorded/notified forest area 22.84% (different concepts).
Alluri Sitharama Raju has AP's largest forest cover (~6,917 sq km); Guntur the least.
AP has India's second-largest mangroves (~418 sq km) in the Godavari & Krishna estuaries (Coringa).
items.mnemonic: 'Ratna Garbha' barytes king = Mangampeta; forest cover 18.46% < notified 22.84%.
items.source: AP Socio-Economic Survey 2024-25 (minerals); ISFR 2023 Vol.2 (AP forests & mangroves)

items.title: Protected Areas, Wetlands, Biodiversity & Hazards
items.body:
## Protected-area network (present-day AP)

- **1 Tiger Reserve** — **Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam (NSTR)**, ~3,727 sq km, among India's largest (Chenchu tribe involved).
- **1 Elephant Reserve** — **Rayala** (Koundinya WLS, Chittoor).
- **1 Biosphere Reserve** — **Seshachalam** (Red Sanders).
- **3 National Parks** — incl. **Sri Venkateswara** (Tirupati) and **Papikonda** (Godavari); **13 Wildlife Sanctuaries**.
- (The old figure of **6 NPs / 21 WLS** is for **undivided AP** — outdated.)

## Wetlands & Ramsar

- **Kolleru Lake** (between Krishna & Godavari deltas) — large freshwater lake, WLS and **Ramsar site**.
- **Pulicat** — brackish coastal **lagoon** shared with **Tamil Nadu** (India's 2nd-largest); **Nellapattu** nearby is a pelican sanctuary.
- **Rollapadu** (Kurnool) — **Great Indian Bustard**.

## Biodiversity & hazards

- AP is in the **Deccan Bio-Geographic Zone**; endemic **Red Sanders**, fauna **Golden Gecko, Indian Bison, Great Indian Bustard**, plus coastal olive-ridley turtles.
- **Hazards:** the coast is among India's most **cyclone-prone** (e.g., **Hudhud, 2014** at Visakhapatnam); recurrent **Godavari/Krishna floods**, **storm surge** and **coastal erosion**; **drought** in Rayalaseema.
keyPoints: Present-day AP: 1 Tiger Reserve (NSTR), 1 Elephant Reserve (Rayala/Koundinya), 1 Biosphere Reserve (Seshachalam), 3 National Parks, 13 WLS.
Kolleru (freshwater, Ramsar) lies between the Krishna & Godavari deltas; Pulicat is a brackish lagoon shared with Tamil Nadu.
Rollapadu (Kurnool) conserves the Great Indian Bustard; Coringa protects Godavari-estuary mangroves.
AP is in the Deccan Bio-Geographic Zone; endemic Red Sanders; fauna include Golden Gecko, Indian Bison, Great Indian Bustard.
The AP coast is highly cyclone-prone (Hudhud 2014 hit Visakhapatnam); floods, storm surge, coastal erosion, and Rayalaseema drought are key hazards.
items.source: AP Socio-Economic Survey 2024-25; AP Protected Areas & Wildlife (2011); disaster records

items.title: Flora, Fauna, Forests & Sanctuaries of Andhra Pradesh
items.body:
## Forests & flora

- **Southern tropical dry deciduous** forest is AP's most widespread type; **teak and bamboo** occur in Godavari and north-coastal forests.
- **Red Sanders (Pterocarpus santalinus)** is **endemic** to the southern Eastern Ghats (**Seshachalam-Palakonda-Lankamalla**); CITES/IUCN-listed and heavily smuggled.
- **Mangroves** (tidal/littoral forest) line the Godavari and Krishna estuaries — **Coringa** is India's **2nd-largest** after the Sundarbans.

## Protected areas (present-day AP)

| Category | Examples |
|---|---|
| Tiger Reserve | **Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam (NSTR)** — among India's largest |
| Biosphere Reserve | **Seshachalam** (Red Sanders) |
| National Parks | **Sri Venkateswara** (Tirupati; Talakona falls), **Papikonda** (Papi Hills, Godavari) |
| Elephant Reserve | **Koundinya WLS** (Chittoor) — AP's only wild elephants |
| Bird sanctuaries | **Nelapattu** (spot-billed pelicans), **Pulicat**, **Rollapadu** (Great Indian Bustard) |

## Endemic & flagship fauna

- **Jerdon's Courser** — critically endangered nocturnal bird, endemic to India, **rediscovered 1986**; only habitat = **Sri Lankamalleswara WLS (Kadapa)**.
- Indian Bison (Gaur), Golden Gecko, olive ridley turtles & estuarine crocodile on the coast.
keyPoints: Southern tropical dry deciduous is AP's most widespread forest type; teak & bamboo occur in Godavari/north-coastal forests.
Red Sanders is endemic to AP's southern Eastern Ghats (Seshachalam-Palakonda-Lankamalla); CITES/IUCN-listed.
Coringa (Godavari estuary) is India's second-largest mangrove after the Sundarbans.
Present-day AP: 1 tiger reserve (NSTR), 1 biosphere reserve (Seshachalam), national parks Sri Venkateswara & Papikonda.
Jerdon's Courser (rediscovered 1986) survives only in Sri Lankamalleswara WLS, Kadapa.
Koundinya WLS (Chittoor) is AP's only sanctuary with wild Asian elephants; Nelapattu is a major pelican breeding site.
items.mnemonic: AP 'firsts': Red Sanders (endemic tree), Coringa (2nd mangrove), Jerdon's Courser (only-habitat bird), Koundinya (only elephants).
items.source: ISFR 2023 Vol.2 (AP); AP Socio-Economic Survey 2024-25; Sri Lankamalleswara WLS, Koundinya WLS, Sri Venkateswara & Papikonda NP (verified)
